I was in the process of evaluating the grammatical validity of the French sentence "Tu n'aurais rien dit à personne." as a correct answer for a question about correctly formed negative conditional past sentences.

## Analysis Completed

The sentence contains a **double negative construction**: "ne...rien" (nothing) combined with "à personne" (to no one). In standard prescriptive French grammar, this is considered incorrect—one should use only one negative element per clause. The correct alternatives would be:
- "Tu n'aurais rien dit." (You wouldn't have said anything)
- "Tu n'aurais dit à personne." (You wouldn't have said [it] to anyone)
